title: Adaptive perturbation probe for cache-hit induced semantic drift
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Objective: Build a lightweight, adaptive probe that detects semantic drift caused specifically by KV/prefix cache hits (i.e., cases where a cache hit changes the downstream model output in a way that meaningfully alters intent or correctness).

Scope: The probe targets our hosted inference fleet and Dedicated clusters where prefix caching is enabled. It should run as both an offline regression job (nightly) and an on-call canary check during rollouts. The probe focuses on short-to-medium prompts (<= 512 tokens) that commonly trigger prefix reuse.

Approach summary:
- Synthetic perturbation generator: create minimal, semantics-preserving perturbations of canonical prompts (whitespace edits, punctuation swaps, paraphrase templates) to exercise different KV-hit/no-hit alignments.
- Hit-conditioned comparison: issue paired requests with identical seeds/config except for forced cache path (hit vs miss) by controlling request routing or simulated warmup. Record token-level alignments and final outputs.
- Multi-metric scoring: combine token-aligned edit distance, ROUGE/L, and an entailment-based semantic equivalence score (NLI model) to quantify meaningful change rather than surface diffs.
- Statistical gating: compute per-prompt z-scores and bootstrap confidence intervals across samples; flag prompts where hit-conditioned divergence exceeds thresholds.
- Cost controls: adaptive sampling that increases probe density only for configurations or model versions with prior instability signals.

Deliverables:
1) Synthetic perturbation library and generator CLI.
2) Hit-conditioned runner able to force cache miss/hit on test paths (integration with shadow-runner + lightweight warmup harness).
3) Scoring toolkit (token-aligner + entailment scorer) and a small dashboard showing per-config anomaly rates.
4) Canary runbook with alert thresholds and remediation steps (rollback, model pin, cache disable for route).

Why this is different: Prior work focuses on large regression suites and hit attribution. This ticket emphasizes an adaptive, low-cost probe that prioritizes semantic equivalence and integrates with rollout gating (canary) rather than heavy nightly batch evaluations. It aims to reduce noisy alerts by focusing on meaning-preserving perturbations and entailment-aware scoring.
acceptance_criteria: Synthetic perturbation generator can produce >= 200 distinct minimal-paraphrase variants per seed prompt
Paired hit/miss runner reproduces controlled cache hit vs miss behavior in test env for at least 90% of trials
Scoring pipeline yields a single composite divergence metric with documented threshold and false-positive rate < 5% on a labelled validation set
Grafana dashboard panel created showing daily anomaly rate per model/config and canary alerting rule (pager duty playbook)
Runbook documented with exact rollback thresholds and links to blocking tickets for disabling cache routing
